main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snow roof slope (rows ~7-51) above a dark timber front wall with a double arched door and two lit windows (rows ~52-76)
top_band: Pale white/light-blue snow roof slope, rows ~8-50, with a thick lighter snow lip along the front eave at rows ~47-51
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: the roof slope is a tall, clearly visible surface of snow clumps in several tones (rows 8-46). A bright snow-lip eave (rows 47-51) forms the front edge, with a dark band and icicles directly under it (row 52 onward) as eave shadow. The vertical timber wall below (rows 52-76) carries an inset arched door with iron straps and windows with snow sills. This matches how the Beodeul reference roofs read as a slope above a front wall, so it is a 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The snow roof uses about 5 steps (white, pale blue, mid blue-grey, shadow blue-grey, dark navy edge), with clumped scallops, per-clump highlights and moss tufts. The wall has vertical wood grain in several browns. Outlines are dark navy next to snow and dark brown next to wood, so they follow the adjacent material rather than a uniform black. The tiles are information-rich (icicles, window glow, door hardware, snow drifts at the base) and comparable to the reference houses, with no large flat fills.
